01.r: The people are told to bring the tithe in.
01.n: A plural command, the causative of the verb 'come': 'cause to come in', so 'bring'.

02.r: Marks the tithe as what is to be brought.
02.n: The object marker has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'all'.

03.r: The whole tithe, nothing held back.

04.r: The tithe the people have been withholding.
04.n: The same word as in the charge two verses before, 'the tithe and the contribution'. Gesenius: tithes, from the noun for 'ten'. It is singular; the KJV, Geneva and DRC make it plural.

05.r: The tithe goes inside the store.
05.n: The brief's lexicon lists 'into' where the limit is actually entered.

06.r: The store-rooms of the temple, where the tithe was kept.
06.n: Literally 'the house of the store': two words, which every translation joins into one.

07.r: What is laid up: stored food and goods.
07.n: Gesenius: properly what is laid up, a store, stock; treasure, store, as of corn, food, provision. The translations render it together with 'house' as one word, 'storehouse'.

08.r: Gives the purpose of bringing the tithe.
08.n: 'And' with the jussive of 'be', 'and let there be', which here expresses purpose. YLT keeps the plain 'And there is'.

09.r: Food to supply those who serve in the LORD's house.
09.n: The brief's lexicon gives prey, food, leaf; Gesenius' senses include an animal torn in pieces, the prey of a wild beast. The KJV's 'meat' is older English for food in general.

s: and put me to the test
11.r: The LORD invites the people to put him to the proof.
11.n: A plural command with 'me' as a suffix. Gesenius: to search out, to examine, to try, to prove, especially metals.

12.r: Softens the command into an invitation.
12.n: Gesenius: a particle used in submissive and modest request, in English by 'now', as a word of entreaty.

13.r: By this act: bringing the whole tithe.

14.r: Marks the words as the LORD's.
14.n: A perfect, 'has said'; YLT renders it 'Said'.

15.r: The personal name of Israel's God.

16.r: The LORD as commander of armies.
16.n: Gesenius: army, host; BDB includes the name of the LORD as God of war. The DRC leaves it out.

17.r: Sets out what the test will show.
17.n: After a challenge, 'if ... not' has the force 'see whether I do not'. YLT turns it into a question, 'Do not I open'.

18.r: Part of 'if I will not': the LORD will open.

19.r: The LORD opens the sky to send blessing.

20.r: The opening is for the people's benefit.

21.r: Marks the windows as what is opened.
21.n: The object marker has no English equivalent; it is counted here with 'the windows of'.

22.r: Openings in the sky through which rain and blessing pour.
22.n: Gesenius: properly lattice-work, and so a window closed with lattice; BDB: lattice, window, sluice. The DRC says 'flood-gates'.

23.n: The word is plural in form; the translations say 'heaven'.

24.r: The LORD empties blessing out on them.
24.n: The brief's lexicon gives 'to make empty, empty out', and 'to pour out or down'. A perfect with 'and', continuing the promise; YLT renders the form literally, 'I have emptied'.

25.r: The blessing is for the people.

26.r: Good gifts from the LORD, here plentiful harvests.
26.n: The brief's lexicon lists blessing, prosperity, and a gift, present. That the blessing is harvest is a reasonable reading of the windows of the sky, which send rain.

27.r: Measures how far the blessing goes.

s: there is no more need of
28.r: With the next word: the blessing outruns any need.
28.n: Literally 'until no enough', a negative particle that BDB calls chiefly poetic for 'not'. Our 'more than enough' follows the JPS; the KJV and ASV read it as 'not room enough to receive it'.

29.r: The point at which there is enough.
29.n: Gesenius: sufficiency, a large enough quantity, and so 'enough'.

_extra.0: καὶ (and): added by the Greek translators at the start; nothing in the Hebrew answers to it.
_extra.11: αὐτοῦ (of it): the Greek says 'its plunder'.

01.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none. εἰσηνέγκατε, 'you brought in'.

04.n: ἐκφόρια, 'produce, yield', where the Hebrew has 'the tithe'.

07.n: εἰς τοὺς θησαυρούς, 'into the treasuries', with no word for 'house'. θησαυρός is the word our register renders 'treasure'.

09.n: ἡ διαρπαγή, 'the plunder': the translators took the Hebrew word in its sense 'prey', which the brief's lexicon lists first.

10.n: The Greek says 'in his house' where the Hebrew has 'in my house'.

13.n: Dictionary form supplied by hand: the matched data gives none.

16.n: παντοκράτωρ, 'Almighty', for 'of hosts'. Printed Γαντοκράτωρ in our Greek text, evidently Παντοκράτωρ.

22.n: καταρράκτης, a waterfall or floodgate; the DRC's 'flood-gates' agrees with this Greek. Printed καταὸάκτας in our Greek text.

29.n: ἕως τοῦ ἱκανωθῆναι, 'until it is enough', with no negative.
